response: {"title":"Requirement-to-module coverage ledger","intervention":"Maintain a compact ledger mapping every explicit requirement to its affected Python module and verification, and do not declare completion while any ledger entry is unmapped or unverified.","claim":"Against no appended instruction, this instruction will increase full-task pass rate on fixed-deadline multi-module Python tasks without increasing median wall time or turns by more than 10%.","mechanism":"Externalizing requirement-to-module coverage reduces working-memory loss and premature completion by making omitted or unverified dispersed requirements auditable before the agent stops.","assumptions":["Task requirements can be represented as a short ledger without consuming material deadline budget.","The agent can identify affected modules and available verification from the repository and task text."],"risks":["The ledger may encode an initially missed or misinterpreted requirement and create false confidence.","Maintaining the ledger may consume scarce time on very short deadlines.","The agent may over-expand scope by mapping implied rather than explicit requirements."],"test_plan":{"experiment":"Randomly assign matched multi-module Python tasks with identical deadlines and agent settings to this appended instruction or no appended instruction.","metrics":["pass_rate","wall_time","turns"],"success_condition":"The intervention arm has a higher full-task pass rate, with median wall_time and turns each no more than 10% above control."},"single_shot_ordinal":1}
